l.i: Nam puri oloris pura gaudent carmina Alios in usus vertere, Illumque debacchantur in Rempublicam Cui laeta[?] parent aequora. Quidiam[?], beate pater, quid vis amplius? Tu numen & praesens Deus, Tu certa spes mortalium vocabere Salusque mundi publica: Ergo thiaras, infulas, ostrum manu Potenti nobis divide. Nam magna quanquam pro te adorti gessimus, Maiora adhuc conabimur, Ipsumque detrahemus e solio Iovem[?], Ut ipse solus imperes.

page.notes: The verse is set in italic type, with the second line of each couplet indented. "Quidiam", "laeta" and "Iovem" are doubtful readings: the scan is faint and the letters are ligated. "ALEXAN:" is the catchword at the right foot, and its final mark is doubtful. The woodcut is an ornament and is not transcribed. Show-through and scan dust are left out.
